About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Physical Design Engineer to own block-to-full-chip implementation and signoff on advanced-node, multi-die 3DIC products. You will drive hierarchical physical design from RTL handoff through tapeout, and lead the multi-physics verification (thermal, mechanical/warpage, and IR/EM) that is unique to stacked-die and chiplet-based systems. This role sits at the intersection of traditional block-level signoff and the emerging discipline of 3D system-level closure.

Key Responsibilities

Hierarchical Physical Design

• Define and execute the hierarchical partitioning strategy: block boundaries, feedthroughs, pin placement, and budgeting across levels of hierarchy.

• Develop and maintain floorplans, power grids, and timing/physical budgets for large multi-block SoCs.

• Own the interface between block owners and top-level integration, including abstract (ILM/ETM) generation, boundary timing, and hierarchical ECO propagation.

• Manage die-to-die partitioning for 3D stacks – assign logic to tiers, plan hybrid-bond / µbump / TSV interfaces, and align inter-die floorplans.

Block-level Implementation & Signoff

• Synthesis: Drive logic synthesis (constraints, DFT insertion, physical-aware synthesis), QoR analysis, and RTL-to-gate correlation.

• Floorplanning: Macro placement, power planning, congestion and timing feasibility, and pin/port optimization.

• Placement & Optimization: Standard-cell placement, timing-driven and congestion-driven optimization, useful-skew and multi-corner/multi-mode

About Formlabs:

Do you want to change how the world creates?

At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.

We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.

Why this role

Most specialty materials are still made the way they have been for decades: weigh, mix in a tank, filter, fill. We think there’s a better way to make them, and we want you to invent it.

Our R&D team creates innovative materials that push the limits of 3D printing, and we need proven manufacturing processes to produce our materials at scale and bring them to market. This isn’t a traditional process engineering role. You won’t be tuning existing equipment or running scale-up checklists. You’ll invent what materials manufacturing looks like next: set up proof of concept pilot processes for new manufacturing technologies, design new mixing and dispersion approaches, and smart control systems that catch a bad lot before it happens. You’ll prototype it, prove it, and put it on the plant floor.

If you’ve ever looked at a production line, thought "there has to be a better way", and then built it, this is your job.

No 3D printing experience required. We need someone who understands how materials behave at scale and can’t stop thinking of better ways to make them.

You might currently be called: Manufacturing Technology Eng
